punchline: Van Gogh tried art dealing, teaching, bookselling and preaching, and when he began painting at twenty-seven, all of it stood behind him as stored experience.
thirty_sec: For most of his life Van Gogh could not tell what would become of him. He was dismissed as an art dealer, then tried teaching, bookselling and preaching. At twenty-seven he began painting seriously. According to David Epstein, each of those apparently failed years had left him something: seeing paintings, understanding human pain, putting a story into a picture.
